patch.objective: Designing data replication and failover: Cloud SQL, Redis clusters

sources.cite: Google Cloud, Professional Data Engineer exam guide v4.2: Designing data processing systems (~22%), Ingesting and processing the data (~25%), Storing the data (~20%), Preparing and using data for analysis (~15%), Maintaining and automating data workloads (~18%)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the PDF on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 3.1 'Planning for storage costs and performance'. The guide does not name partitioning or clustering. (read for this round by an earlier pass on 2026-11-17)

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: Replication lag
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: causes include an undersized replica, 'long-running replica queries' that block replay, and an overloaded replica; metrics replica_lag and network_lag ('If network_lag is negligible but replica_lag is high, the replica is the bottleneck'); fixes: right-size the replica, tune max_standby_streaming_delay (about 30-60 seconds) and check pg_stat_database_conflicts, 'Use different replicas for OLTP and OLAP'. The 'Manage read replicas' page (read 2026-11-18): 'Promoting a read replica stops replication and converts the instance to a standalone Cloud SQL primary instance'; it describes no way back to a replica.
